stem: A straight playground slide makes a \(30^{\circ}\) angle with the level ground, as shown. The sliding surface is 3.6 meters long. How high above the ground, in meters, is the top of the slide?
solution: The slide, the ground, and the vertical height form a 30°-60°-90° triangle with hypotenuse 3.6.
The side opposite the \(30^{\circ}\) angle is half the hypotenuse: \(h = \frac{3.6}{2} = 1.8\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('G','T')-Rational('3.6'))<0.01 and abs(ang('T','G','F')-30)<0.1 and abs(ang('G','F','T')-90)<0.1
ans=Rational('3.6')*sin(pi/6)
assert abs(P['T'][1]-ans)<0.01
assert all(Rational(s)==ans==Rational(9,5) for s in spr_answers)
